result.topic_en: Euler adapts the forms pp − nqq and npp − qq to divisor classes of the form 4ni ± a, sets out what remains to be proved (that 4ni ± α contains all primes that are never divisors), and states corollaries on the multiplicative structure of the residues a and the excluded values α.
result.transcription:

quae est forma nostra inuersa $npp - qq$. Hinc igitur intelligitur, si fuerit $Df$ numerus formae $pp - nqq$, tum eo ipso formulam $Dh$ fore numerum formae $npp - qq$.

II. Accommodemus haec etiam ad eam formam diuisorum, quam olim exhibui; ac primo quidem si fuerit $D = pp - nqq$, pro casibus quibus $q$ est numerus par, ideoque $qq$ formae $4i$, fiet $D = pp - 4ni$; vnde si ponatur $D = 4ni + a$, ob $pp > 4ni$, si ponatur $pp = 4nk + b$ prodibit talis forma: $D = 4ni + b$, ita vt sit $a = b$, ideoque omnes numeros quadratos ad $4n$ primos in se complectatur. Sin autem sit $q$ numerus impar, ideoque $qq$ formae $4i + 1$, fiet $D = pp - n - 4ni$, positoque iterum $pp = 4nk + b$, prodit $D = 4ni + b - n$, ita vt hoc casu sit $a = b - n$, vbi $b$ denotare potest omnes numeros quadratos, vel residua inde orta. Simili modo si fuerit $D = npp - qq$, euidens est, valores pro $a$ hinc prodituros praecedentium fore negatiuos, ita vt $a$ comprehendat omnes numeros quadratos, deinde etiam omnes numeros formae $pp - n$, tam positiue quam negatiue sumtos; quamobrem forma omnium diuisorum ita exhiberi poterit, vt sit $4ni \pm a$, forma autem pro numeris ex classe diuisorum exclusis erit $4ni \pm \alpha$, quorum multitudo aequalis est priori, scilicet $\alpha$ semper totidem sortietur valores, quot habet littera $a$.

III. Quo igitur etiam in hoc genere nihil amplius desiderari queat, id tantum superest, vt demonstretur, formam

237

nam posteriorem $4ni \pm \alpha$ omnes plane continere numeros primos, qui nunquam esse queant diuisores vllius numeri vel formae $pp - nqq$, vel $npp - qq$.

Corollarium 1.

§. 15. De his binis formulis: $4ni \pm a$ et $4ni \pm \alpha$, quarum illa omnes diuisores inuoluit, haec vero excludit, eadem valent, quae ante sunt tradita. Scilicet si $a, a', a''$, etc. ad priorem classem pertineant, ibidem quoque reperientur tam omnes potestates quam producta ex binis pluribusue horum numerorum; tum vero si $\alpha$ sit numerus posterioris classis, ibidem quoque occurrent omnes numeri $a\alpha$, $a'\alpha$, $a''\alpha$, etc., ita vt multitudo horum numerorum minor esse nequeat quam prioris classis.

Corollarium 2.

§. 16. Quoniam littera $a$ complectitur omnia quadrata, ante omnia eius valor erit $= 1$, tum vero etiam $9$, $25$, etc. nisi numerus $n$ habeat diuisorem vel $3$, vel $5$, etc. His enim casibus ista quadrata excludi oportet, quia alioquin forma $4ni \pm a$ numerus primus fieri non posset.

Scholion.

§. 17. His igitur generalibus praeceptis expositis omnia clariora euadent, si casus particulares euoluamus; hic enim plura adhuc occurrent, quae in genere attingere non licuit. Sufficiet autem id in aliquibus exemplis ostendisse, quibus pertractatis non difficile erit tabulam construere, quae pro omnibus casibus formas diuisorum primorum exhibeat.

Exem-

items.quote: si fuerit $Df$ numerus formae $pp - nqq$, tum eo ipso formulam $Dh$ fore numerum formae $npp - qq$.
items.english: If Df is a number of the form pp − nqq, then by that very fact the formula Dh will be a number of the form npp − qq.

items.quote: forma omnium diuisorum ita exhiberi poterit, vt sit $4ni \pm a$, forma autem pro numeris ex classe diuisorum exclusis erit $4ni \pm \alpha$, quorum multitudo aequalis est priori, scilicet $\alpha$ semper totidem sortietur valores, quot habet littera $a$.
items.english: The form of all divisors can be exhibited as 4ni ± a, while the form for the numbers excluded from the class of divisors will be 4ni ± α, whose number of values equals that of the former; that is, α will always take as many values as the letter a has.

items.quote: id tantum superest, vt demonstretur, formam nam posteriorem $4ni \pm \alpha$ omnes plane continere numeros primos, qui nunquam esse queant diuisores vllius numeri vel formae $pp - nqq$, vel $npp - qq$.
items.english: It only remains to be demonstrated that the latter form 4ni ± α contains absolutely all prime numbers which can never be divisors of any number of the form pp − nqq or npp − qq.

items.quote: si $a, a', a''$, etc. ad priorem classem pertineant, ibidem quoque reperientur tam omnes potestates quam producta ex binis pluribusue horum numerorum; tum vero si $\alpha$ sit numerus posterioris classis, ibidem quoque occurrent omnes numeri $a\alpha$, $a'\alpha$, $a''\alpha$, etc., ita vt multitudo horum numerorum minor esse nequeat quam prioris classis.
items.english: If a, a', a'', etc. belong to the former class, then all their powers, and the products of two or more of these numbers, will also be found there. And if α is a number of the latter class, then all the numbers aα, a'α, a''α, etc. will also occur there, so that the number of these values cannot be smaller than that of the former class.

items.quote: Quoniam littera $a$ complectitur omnia quadrata, ante omnia eius valor erit $= 1$, tum vero etiam $9$, $25$, etc. nisi numerus $n$ habeat diuisorem vel $3$, vel $5$, etc.
items.english: Since the letter a includes all squares, first of all its value will be 1, and then also 9, 25, etc., unless the number n has the divisor 3 or 5, etc. (in those cases these squares must be excluded, since otherwise the form 4ni ± a could not be a prime).

items.quote: Sufficiet autem id in aliquibus exemplis ostendisse, quibus pertractatis non difficile erit tabulam construere, quae pro omnibus casibus formas diuisorum primorum exhibeat.
items.english: It will suffice to show this in some examples; once these have been worked through, it will not be difficult to construct a table giving the forms of the prime divisors for all cases.
